<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

<!-- PR title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] muse-spark: Fuse the pooler all-gather into the pre-expert norm and NVFP4 quant -->

## Motivation

In a decode MoE layer two streams run after the attention boundary, and the experts' first GEMM starts when both have finished:

- main stream: the pre-expert projection (pooler) on this rank's column slice, the all-gather of the slices, then the pre-expert RMSNorm + static NVFP4 quant;
- router stream: the router GEMM and the top-8 routing.

This PR fuses the gather, the norm and the quant, so the main stream is one launch and one bf16 round trip shorter. It also takes the pooler gather path on SM107 and up to 1024 tokens at TP4.

**The gain shows only when the main stream gates the experts.** When the router stream finishes last, the experts wait for the router regardless, and this PR does not move them; the saving appears once the router stream is shortened.

## Modifications

- `all_gather_norm_fp4_quant.cuh` (new): multicast push of the local slice on the `CustomAllReduceV2` push plane, Lamport poll of each 16-element block in `norm_fp4_quant`'s thread map, then the RMSNorm and the static-scale NVFP4 quant of `norm_fp4_quant.cuh` on the gathered row in registers. fp4 / scale factors are bitwise those of the all-gather + `fused_norm_fp4_quant_static`.
- `muse_spark_all_gather.py`: the op (`all_gather_norm_fp4_quant`) and its shape check. `gemm_ag_supported(..., pooler=True)` is the pre-expert projection's rule: TP4 / TP8 on SM103 or SM107, up to `POOLER_TP4_MAX_TOKENS = 1024` at TP4 (the 8 MB push slot). The unpooler keeps the SM103-only rule and `MAX_TOKENS`.
- `muse_spark_gemm_ag.py`: `gemm_ag_norm_fp4_quant`, the local slice GEMM followed by the fused kernel.
- `muse_spark.py`: `MuseSpark1xMoE` passes the fused FP4 / scale-factor tuple to the experts as `prepared_input` when the experts take static-scale NVFP4 input through the pre-expert norm.

## Accuracy Tests

<!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. -->

Outputs are bitwise those of the all-gather + `fused_norm_fp4_quant_static`, so model outputs do not change.

Muse Spark Open + this PR, DFlash (real acceptance), sgl-eval with T=1.0, top_p=1.0, top_k=64, xhigh reasoning; GSM8K max 65K tokens, AIME26 30 problems x 16 repeats, max 131K tokens.

| GPU | TP | GSM8K | AIME26 pass@1 | AIME26 pass@16 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GB300 | 4 | 97.50% | 96.88% | 100% |
| SM107 | 4 | 97.80% | 96.25% | 100% |

<details>
<summary>Kernel tests</summary>

`test_muse_spark_all_gather_norm_fp4_quant.py`, bitwise on every rank against the push-plane all-gather + `fused_norm_fp4_quant_static` (rows, fp4 and scale factors, with and without the gathered rows): M in {1, 64, 65, 200, 1024} on a 64-block push plane (one block, one row per block, rows looping over blocks, the full 8 MB slot), four rounds of fresh inputs so both push-plane phases carry new data, eager and CUDA graph replay; failures are collected across ranks before raising.

- SM107: 10 / 10 at TP4 and at TP8.
- GB300 TP4: bitwise for M = 1-1024 (including 147, 148, 295 and 589), with and without the norm weight; a 200-iteration phase stress interleaved with the custom all-reduce; CUDA graph replay.

</details>

## Speed Tests and Profiling

<!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. -->

**Setup.** Base = our Muse decode stack, this PR = the same stack + this PR; FlashInfer autotune off and per-token NVFP4 activation off on both sides.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.
[by Claude Code] This review is done by agents. Please feel free to disagree if they do not make sense.

[by Claude Code] **Severity: style | Confidence: High**

**Issue**

`_fuse_ag_norm_quant` adds `getattr(self.experts, "use_marlin", False)`. SGLang does not allow defensive `getattr`. The check runs only after `self.nvfp4_checkpoint`, so on GPU `self.experts` is a `MuseSpark1xFp4Experts`, which always sets `use_marlin` in `__init__`. The next line already reads `self.experts.quant_config` directly.

**Fix**

Read the field directly:

```python
and not self.experts.use_marlin
```

If you want the type to be explicit, narrow with `isinstance(self.experts, MuseSpark1xFp4Experts)` first.

[by Claude Code] **Severity: style | Confidence: High**

**Issue**

This PR conflicts with main in `gemm_ag_supported`. #47782 changed the SM103 check in this function to `current_arch().is_sm(10, 3)`. The pooler rule adds two `torch.cuda.get_device_capability(x.device)` checks (here and in the `n in (4096, 8192)` branch). A plain conflict resolution leaves the function with two styles of arch query.

**Fix**

When you rebase, use the `sglang.kernels.arch` helper for both checks, for example:

```python
sm_ok = current_arch().is_sm(10, 3) or (pooler and current_arch().is_sm(10, 7))
```

Then reuse `sm_ok` in both places instead of the `archs` tuple.

[by Claude Code] **Severity: style | Confidence: Medium**

**Issue**

This test registers in `stage="extra-b"`. The other Muse Spark kernel tests use `base-b-kernel-unit`, including `test_muse_spark_rmsnorm_nvfp4_quant.py` and `test_muse_spark_moe_finalize_all_reduce.py` on the same `4-gpu-b200` runner. PR Test Extra does not gate a normal merge.

**Why it matters**

This kernel copies the thread map and reduction order of `norm_fp4_quant.cuh` and reuses the CustomAllReduceV2 push-plane phase protocol. A later PR that changes either one can break the bitwise contract here without failing a required check.

**Fix**

Register it in `base-b-kernel-unit`. If the 90 s budget is the concern, trim `ROWS`.

+"""Muse Spark pooler gather fused with the pre-expert RMSNorm + static NVFP4 quant.
+
+The fused kernel must stay bitwise equal, on every rank, to the push-plane all-gather
+followed by fused_norm_fp4_quant_static: when rows outnumber the work blocks, when the
+gathered rows fill the push slot, across both push-plane phases with fresh data, and when
+replayed from a CUDA graph as served.
+
+Run with ``python <this file>``; it relaunches under torchrun on 4 and 8 GPUs.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import atexit
+import logging
+import os
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+import torch.distributed as dist
+
+import sglang.srt.distributed.parallel_state as ps
+from sglang.kernels.jit.utils import cache_once
+from sglang.kernels.ops.communication.muse_spark_all_gather import (
+    all_gather,
+    all_gather_norm_fp4_quant,
+)
+from sglang.kernels.ops.layernorm.muse_spark_rmsnorm_nvfp4_quant import (
+    fused_norm_fp4_quant_static,
+)
+from sglang.srt.distributed.comm_cleanup import register_comm_cleanup
+from sglang.srt.distributed.device_communicators.custom_all_reduce_v2 import (
+    CustomAllReduceV2,
+)
+from sglang.srt.runtime_context import get_parallel
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cuda_ci
+from sglang.test.kernels.utils import multigpu_pytest_main
+
+register_cuda_ci(est_time=90, stage="extra-b", runner_config="4-gpu-b200")
+
+N = 4096
+EPS = 1e-6
+PUSH_BYTES = 8 * 1024 * 1024
+# The kernel launches min(rows, PUSH_BLOCKS) blocks: 1 row leaves counters past the grid to
+# block 0, 64 rows give one row per block, 65 and 200 loop rows per block (both reduction
+# buffers), and 1024 rows of N bf16 fill PUSH_BYTES.
+PUSH_BLOCKS = 64
+ROWS = [1, 64, 65, 200, 1024]
+# Each round launches three push-plane kernels, so every launch alternates the phase half;
+# four rounds of fresh data put each kernel on both halves with new payloads.
+ROUNDS = 4
+
+
+@cache_once
+def _init():
+    local_rank = int(os.environ["LOCAL_RANK"])
+    world_size = int(os.environ["WORLD_SIZE"])
+    torch.cuda.set_device(local_rank)
+    dist.init_process_group(backend="gloo")
+    ps._WORLD = coord = ps.init_world_group(
+        ranks=list(range(world_size)), local_rank=local_rank, backend="nccl"
+    )
+    get_parallel().override_permanently(world_group=coord)
+    atexit.register(dist.destroy_process_group)
+    logging.disable(logging.INFO)
+    comm = CustomAllReduceV2(
+        coord.cpu_group,
+        torch.device(f"cuda:{local_rank}"),
+        max_pull_size=0,
+        max_pull_blocks=0,
+        max_push_size=PUSH_BYTES,
+        max_push_blocks=PUSH_BLOCKS,
+    )
+    assert not comm.disabled
+    register_comm_cleanup(comm)
+    return coord, comm
+
+
+def _assert_all_ranks(failures: list[str], context: str) -> None:
+    """Raise on every rank if any rank failed, so no rank is left waiting in a collective."""
+    per_rank = [None] * dist.get_world_size()
+    dist.all_gather_object(per_rank, failures)
+    report = [f"rank {r}: {f}" for r, fs in enumerate(per_rank) for f in fs]
+    assert not report, f"{context}: " + "; ".join(report)
+
+
+def _bits(t: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    return t.view(torch.uint8)
+
+
+def _local_rows(coord, rows: int, seed: int) -> torch.Tensor:
+    g = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(seed * 64 + coord.rank)
+    local = torch.randn(rows, N // coord.world_size, device="cuda", generator=g) * 2
+    local[:, ::97] = 0  # exact zeros travel through the push plane's +0 marker remap
+    return local.bfloat16()
+
+
+def _run_step(comm, local, weight, global_scale):
+    """The fused op with and without the gathered rows, then the unfused all-gather."""
+    rows, fp4, sf = all_gather_norm_fp4_quant(
+        comm, local, weight, EPS, global_scale, write_rows=True
+    )
+    _, fp4_no_rows, sf_no_rows = all_gather_norm_fp4_quant(
+        comm, local, weight, EPS, global_scale, write_rows=False
+    )
+    ref_rows = torch.empty(local.shape[0], N, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
+    all_gather(comm, local, ref_rows)
+    return rows, fp4, sf, fp4_no_rows, sf_no_rows, ref_rows
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("use_graph", [False, True], ids=["eager", "graph"])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("rows", ROWS)
+def test_matches_all_gather_then_norm_quant(rows: int, use_graph: bool):
+    coord, comm = _init()
+    if not comm.has_multicast:
+        pytest.skip("needs a multicast-capable push plane")
+    shared = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(rows)
+    weight = (1 + 0.1 * torch.randn(N, device="cuda", generator=shared)).bfloat16()
+    global_scale = torch.tensor([448.0 * 6.0 / 3.5], device="cuda")
+    local = _local_rows(coord, rows, seed=0)
+
+    side = torch.cuda.Stream()
+    side.wait_stream(torch.cuda.current_stream())
+    with torch.cuda.stream(side):
+        outs = _run_step(comm, local, weight, global_scale)
+        if use_graph:
+            torch.cuda.synchronize()
+            graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+            with comm.capture():
+                with torch.cuda.graph(graph, stream=side):
+                    outs = _run_step(comm, local, weight, global_scale)
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+
+    for rnd in range(ROUNDS):
+        local.copy_(_local_rows(coord, rows, seed=rnd + 1))
+        if use_graph:
+            graph.replay()
+        else:
+            outs = _run_step(comm, local, weight, global_scale)
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+        got_rows, fp4, sf, fp4_no_rows, sf_no_rows, ref_rows = outs
+        ref_fp4, ref_sf = fused_norm_fp4_quant_static(
+            ref_rows, weight, EPS, global_scale
+        )
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+        checks = (
+            ("rows", got_rows, ref_rows),
+            ("fp4", fp4, ref_fp4),
+            ("sf", sf, ref_sf),
+            ("fp4 (no rows)", fp4_no_rows, ref_fp4),
+            ("sf (no rows)", sf_no_rows, ref_sf),
+        )
+        failures = [
+            f"{name}: {int((_bits(a) != _bits(b)).sum())} bytes differ"
+            for name, a, b in checks
+            if not torch.equal(_bits(a), _bits(b))
+        ]
+        _assert_all_ranks(failures, f"round {rnd}")
+        # Every rank quantizes the same gathered rows, so the outputs must agree across ranks.
+        peers = [torch.empty_like(fp4) for _ in range(coord.world_size)]
+        dist.all_gather(peers, fp4, group=coord.device_group)
+        _assert_all_ranks(
+            [
+                f"fp4 differs from rank {r}"
+                for r, p in enumerate(peers)
+                if not torch.equal(p, fp4)
+            ],
+            f"round {rnd} cross-rank",
+        )
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    multigpu_pytest_main(__name__, __file__, num_gpus=(4, 8))

inline_comments.body:
[by Claude Code] **Severity: style | Confidence: High**

**Issue**

`_fuse_ag_norm_quant` adds `getattr(self.experts, "use_marlin", False)`. SGLang does not allow defensive `getattr`. The check runs only after `self.nvfp4_checkpoint`, so on GPU `self.experts` is a `MuseSpark1xFp4Experts`, which always sets `use_marlin` in `__init__`. The next line already reads `self.experts.quant_config` directly.

**Fix**

Read the field directly:

```python
and not self.experts.use_marlin
```

If you want the type to be explicit, narrow with `isinstance(self.experts, MuseSpark1xFp4Experts)` first.

**Issue**

This PR conflicts with main in `gemm_ag_supported`. #47782 changed the SM103 check in this function to `current_arch().is_sm(10, 3)`. The pooler rule adds two `torch.cuda.get_device_capability(x.device)` checks (here and in the `n in (4096, 8192)` branch). A plain conflict resolution leaves the function with two styles of arch query.

**Fix**

When you rebase, use the `sglang.kernels.arch` helper for both checks, for example:

```python
sm_ok = current_arch().is_sm(10, 3) or (pooler and current_arch().is_sm(10, 7))
```

Then reuse `sm_ok` in both places instead of the `archs` tuple.

[by Claude Code] **Severity: style | Confidence: Medium**

**Issue**

This test registers in `stage="extra-b"`. The other Muse Spark kernel tests use `base-b-kernel-unit`, including `test_muse_spark_rmsnorm_nvfp4_quant.py` and `test_muse_spark_moe_finalize_all_reduce.py` on the same `4-gpu-b200` runner. PR Test Extra does not gate a normal merge.

**Why it matters**

This kernel copies the thread map and reduction order of `norm_fp4_quant.cuh` and reuses the CustomAllReduceV2 push-plane phase protocol. A later PR that changes either one can break the bitwise contract here without failing a required check.

**Fix**

Register it in `base-b-kernel-unit`. If the 90 s budget is the concern, trim `ROWS`.
